clue.text: Hanging out on rock in a wind, needing a hat

parts.note: a saxophone is a wind instrument
taken as written
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A climber dangles from a rock face in a gale, wishing they had brought a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxatile is a botanical and zoological term for living or growing among rocks.

clue.text: Noticed Henry's trousers hung up: that's drawing a snort from Hamish?

definitions.note: describes the thing by its use: something a Scot sniffs up

indicators.note: in a down entry, hanging something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards
used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance, plus the S of the possessive
noticed means seen

explanation.surface: Someone spots Henry pocketing an item, prompting a Scot named Hamish to snort.
explanation.walkthrough: H(SEEN)S is read upwards to give SNEESH. Hamish is a typically Scottish name, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneesh is a Scots word for snuff, the powdered tobacco taken by sniffing it up the nose.

clue.text: Axes one who'd do a bit less Queen: graduate music maker

parts.note: the x and y axes of a graph

indicators.note: less means without, so the royal abbreviation is subtracted from the craftsman

parts.note: a lorimer makes bits, spurs and other metal parts of a horse's harness
ER is Elizabeth Regina
Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A queen's craftsman does less work and goes off to graduate in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who'd do a bit' sounds like someone doing a small share of work; here it is a maker of horses' bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylorimba is a percussion instrument combining the ranges of xylophone and marimba, so it produces music.

clue.text: Up to banks with one billion to make pick

indicators.note: banks are the sides of a river, so one word forms the sides around the others

parts.note: till means up to, as in till Friday
W is the abbreviation for with
Roman numeral one
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Someone deposits a billion with the banks to make a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the financial sense but is a container signal; 'pick' looks like a verb meaning choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A twibill is a double-bladed tool like a mattock, a kind of digging pick.

clue.text: Informal power cycle for exercising

indicators.note: exercising puts something through its paces, working it about until its parts are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone uses an exercise bike as a cheap way to generate electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Leccy is British slang for electricity, the power from the mains supply.

clue.text: Cheers welcoming trumpeter for one's race in Africa

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
the trumpeter is a species of swan

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers on a trumpet player at a race meeting in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumpeter' suggests a musician but is the trumpeter swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tswana are a Bantu-speaking people of Botswana and South Africa, an African ethnic group.

clue.text: Vilification of Republican's opponent perhaps upset resolve of SNP?

definitions.note: the SNP is the Scottish National Party, so this flags a Scots word

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses the reading order

parts.note: to throw mud is to vilify
a Democrat, or Dem, opposes a Republican in US politics, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Mudslinging aimed at a US Republican's rival upsets the determination of Scottish nationalists.
explanation.walkthrough: MUD + DEMS reads MUDDEMS, which upturned gives SMEDDUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Smeddum is a Scots word for spirit, mettle or determination, matching resolve as a noun.

clue.text: Forgotten calls to pack in promotion of beer by international rugby team

indicators.note: promotion lifts something out of its rank and moves it up, here to the top of a down entry

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Wales plays international rugby union

explanation.surface: A beer brand sponsors the Welsh rugby team, so the advertising calls to drink up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, promotion means moving up to the top, so the beer climbs from inside the team name to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Alew is an obsolete form of halloo, a shout or call, so alews are calls now forgotten.

clue.text: Moulding of netball player into star

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: astral means relating to the stars
GA is goal attack, a netball position

explanation.surface: A sculpture shows a netball player turned into a star.
explanation.definitionFit: An astragal is a small convex moulding with a rounded profile, used in architecture and on columns.

clue.text: Fungi's russet gills oddly ignored previously

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-placed letters keeps only those in even positions

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A mushroom's reddish-brown gills are overlooked before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ustilago is a genus of smut fungi that attack cereal grasses, so it names a group of fungi.

clue.text: Making plain cake, one's initially smothered in sticky stuff

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the sticky stuff

parts.note: an eclair is a cream-filled pastry cake
cement is an adhesive
I for one, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: first letter of smothered

explanation.surface: A cake-maker clarifies their method: the cake is smothered in something sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smothered' looks like the container signal but only supplies its first letter; 'in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclaircissement is a French borrowing meaning clarification or explanation, the act of clearing something up.

clue.text: With ill temper, briefly waves when breaking with girl

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: surf is breaking waves
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone sulks and waves briefly as they break up with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Surlily is the adverb of surly, describing how a bad-tempered, rude person acts.

clue.text: Working hard, go off, turning over excellent cases

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the attempt is removed from the effort

parts.note: industry is diligent, hard work
a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: turning something over flips its order end to end

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A diligent worker gives up and overturns some excellent legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' suggests lawsuits, but here means protective coverings. A1 for excellent is written with I standing in for the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Indusia are protective membranes or sheaths, for example covering fern spore clusters, so they are cases.

clue.text: One's getting vial, up for replacing ancient basins

parts.note: one is, said in the first person, becomes I'm

indicators.note: replacing here means placing again, putting the letters back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone brings in a small bottle to replace old washbasins.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman houses an impluvium was the sunken tank in the atrium collecting rainwater; impluvia is its plural.

clue.text: I kicked up in dismay, finding info brought to screen

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to vex is to trouble or dismay
taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down entry means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to toe is to kick with the toe

explanation.surface: Someone kicks out in frustration at the information appearing on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' applies to the kicking only, since it is a down entry; 'in dismay' looks like a phrase but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Videotex is a system delivering text and data to a television or computer screen, like Prestel or Ceefax.

clue.text: A necessity for going around park improbably short distances once

indicators.note: going around turns about, so the concealed letters are read right to left
a necessity for something is a part it needs, so the answer is a part of the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the second letter of park into the start of improbably

explanation.surface: A sign claims a park can only be walked round in improbably tiny distances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'park' looks like fodder for an anagram signalled by 'improbably'; instead the answer lies backwards across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikra is an old plural of mikron, a former spelling of micron, a millionth of a metre, so tiny lengths.

clue.text: Character often dropped in Black Sea had idea ultimately to become avenging tribesman

indicators.note: in places the letter's name inside the selected letters
ultimately points to the final letter of each word

parts.note: the last letters of black, sea, had and idea
aitch is the letter H, famously dropped in many English accents

explanation.surface: Someone on the Black Sea gets an idea of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The character is a letter, not a person: the one Cockney speakers drop at the start of words, spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian Aboriginal culture a kadaitcha is a man who carries out ritual vengeance, often by pointing a bone.

clue.text: Short shock about no good work reflecting Italian might have blown it?

definitions.note: describes the thing as something an Italian blows

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters are read back to front
about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the other pieces
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to shock is to amaze
NG is short for no good
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An Italian blows a short sharp shock about a piece of work that's no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown it' suggests failing, but means playing the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zampogna is an Italian bagpipe, an instrument an Italian piper would blow into.

clue.text: Some vocal music prepared with loudspeaker backing

parts.note: à la, as on a menu, means prepared in the manner of or with

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a public address system

explanation.surface: A singer has rehearsed with a speaker system playing behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaap is the slow improvised opening of a raga in Indian classical music, often sung.

clue.text: Leg for one that's crawling, or for all ages?

parts.note: per means for each, as in per day
an aeon is an immeasurably long time

explanation.surface: A riddle about a crawling creature's legs, or something lasting for all time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg' is a section, as in a leg of a journey: the body section of a crawling crustacean.
explanation.definitionFit: The peraeon is the thorax of a crustacean, the body section bearing its walking legs.

clue.text: Old warships making one area of ice or reversing

indicators.note: reversing means the word goes in back to front
making one thing into another swaps the first pair of letters for the second

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ancient warships pass through an area of ice or turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: In DIAMONDS the IA becomes RO. Ice here is slang for diamonds, not frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dromond was a large fast galley of the Byzantine and medieval navies.

clue.text: Ices with something skimmed

cum is Latin for with, as in kitchen-cum-diner

explanation.surface: Someone serves frozen desserts with the cream skimmed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ices' looks like frozen desserts; it is underworld slang for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Offscum is the scum or refuse skimmed off a liquid, hence dregs.

clue.text: Respectful title of house music player entering into the spirit

HO is the abbreviation for house
a disc jockey plays music

explanation.definitionFit: Khodja is a title of respect for a teacher or scholar in Turkey and the Muslim world.

clue.text: Aussie native put in pocket gold pair of spectacles

the two round lenses of spectacles look like a pair of Os

clue.text: Squat alongside, beneath bar after climbing

climbing goes upward, which in a down entry reverses the reading

parts.note: bar and but both mean except
by means beside

explanation.surface: Someone crouches next to a bar after a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, squat and tubby both describe someone short and thickset in build.

clue.text: "Nobby's canned tuna", maybe no longer fashionable

clue.text: Working hard in support of sporting attempt

H is hard on pencil grades

clue.text: Plant hormone in Cecil, laid out after babble

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Rating Angus's one grand? No longer paying

clue.text: Tent for Indian's collection of fake items?

the suffix -iana marks a collection of things, as in Victoriana
surface padding completing the phrase about a collection

explanation.definitionFit: A shamiana is a large decorated canopy or marquee used in India for ceremonies.
